requirements: Define one shared runtime attribution packet across tool events, artifacts, receipts, and usage records with run/attempt/thread/node identity plus provider/account anchors.
Treat `attempt_id` as local runtime anchor, `provider_attempt_ref` as provider/runtime bridge, `usage_event_ref` as usage bridge, and receipt refs as external side-effect lineage bridge.
Make runtime-artifact envelopes attempt-native by default and include canonical artifact identity, runtime attribution, routing refs, and payload metadata.
Split open behavior into path-native `OpenFile` for workspace docs and identity-native `OpenSubject` for artifact/runtime/report targets.
Normalize routing/deep-link/navigation around one internal target payload used by in-app commands and serialized `resume_url` forms.
Add a compact canonical navigation command family so surface-specific open/show commands become wrappers over one shared target model.
decisions: Storage/runtime docs should own the shared attribution contract; tool/artifact docs consume it instead of maintaining partial local identity models.
Timestamp/run/thread fallbacks for usage routing are compatibility-only when canonical bridge refs are absent.
Keep `artifact_id` as artifact-object identity while lineage helpers (`logical_artifact_id`, `linked_artifact_id`) remain non-primary.
Use preview subject identity pattern (`doc:` / `artifact:`) as the basis for generalized open-by-identity routing.
Preserve domain-specific open actions for UX clarity, but bind them to shared route/subject payload semantics.
data_shapes: Shared attribution packet fields: `run_id`, optional `attempt_id`, `thread_id`, `node_id`, `artifact_id`, `usage_event_ref`, `provider_attempt_ref`, plus effective runtime/account identity and optional repo/worktree/branch + external operation refs.

Runtime-artifact envelope minimum: artifact identity (`artifact_id`, `artifact_kind`, optional logical/linked IDs), runtime attribution (`run_id`, optional thread/node/attempt/execution/provider/usage), routing refs, and payload metadata (`created_at_utc`, summary/detail/content refs).
Open-subject model: `OpenSubject { subject_id, target_group?, open_mode?, location? }` with subject families for docs, artifacts, attempts, safe points, remediations, and scheduler passes.
Canonical route payload minimum includes target kind plus contextual pivots such as project/run/thread/subject/object/tab/inspector and optional file line/range.
routing_rules: Identity opens resolve in order: canonical file-backed document, else artifact/generated target, else routed surface focus with identity preserved, else typed open error.
Usage/cost pivots should prefer `usage_event_ref` when present rather than heuristic timestamp joins.
Provider-backed tool/runtime traces should propagate `provider_attempt_ref` when available to keep traceability intact.
Command palette/search/artifact pivots/blocked resumes should all resolve through the same navigation target model, not parallel deep-link stacks.
verification_rules: Bridge refs must not drift into replacement primary keys; `attempt_id` remains canonical local execution identity.
Runtime-artifact docs must not rely on artifact-local identity alone when cross-surface receipt/usage/runtime joins are required.
Wiring and gate schemas must be able to represent canonical runtime actions, admissibility constraints, freshness/revalidation checks, and deprecated/tombstoned command status.
Command/event extraction must avoid false positives from stale examples or filename-like tokens.
owner_consumer_obligations: Owner docs must explicitly publish precedence and join rules for `attempt_id`, `provider_attempt_ref`, `usage_event_ref`, and receipt lineage refs.
FileManager/Editor/Artifacts/Orchestrator consumers should use shared subject/route contracts instead of reconstructing paths ad hoc.
UI command catalog, wiring matrix, and dispatcher rules should share one enforceable command/route boundary including reverse-coverage expectations.
stale_retirement_items: Retire path-only assumptions for all open actions now that runtime/generated identity targets are first-class.
Retire treating `tool.invoked` as analytics-only where runtime attribution is required for side-effect-bearing traces.
Retire artifact packet dependence on legacy `task_id` as primary execution anchor.
open_questions: Which owner doc is canonical for route payload/target-kind schema and serialized `resume_url` mapping?
How should deprecated command families and wildcard requirements be represented in catalog/matrix schemas and gates?
What durable storage/event contract should `attention_required` use to align gate evidence with runtime behavior?
How should startup recovery ownership be unified across policy/executor/storage/HITL docs?
process_defects: Runtime identity, routing, and command ownership remain fragmented across owner docs, causing drift and addendum-heavy reconciliation.
Wiring/gate verification remains underpowered relative to runtime-era command and routing semantics.
Glossary/Crosswalk structural weaknesses continue to block reliable term and primitive ownership resolution.
Artifact/file/open contracts still lag the attempt/project/generated identity model needed for deterministic routing.
doc_hints: Codify shared runtime attribution packet and bridge-field precedence in canonical contracts/storage owners, then reference from tool/artifact/usage docs.
Promote runtime-artifact envelope minimum contract in artifact owner docs with explicit attempt-native semantics.
Introduce canonical `OpenSubject` + route payload owners and align FileManager/Final GUI/Command Catalog wording accordingly.
Upgrade wiring/gate schemas for runtime command admissibility, freshness checks, reverse coverage, and deprecation handling.
Repair Glossary/Crosswalk ownership and routing index integrity before further downstream reconciliations.
